title: CuFe 2 O 4  spinel-based tyrosinase biointerface for electrochemical tyrosine detection
content: Tyrosine is an essential aromatic amino acid, and its abnormal levels are associated with metabolic disorders such as tyrosinemia, highlighting the need for a reliable and rapid detection method. In this work, an enzymatic electrochemical biosensor based on a CuFe2O4-modified tyrosinase screen-printed carbon electrode (SPCE) was developed for the sensitive detection of tyrosine. Structural and morphological analyses of the CuFe2O4 material revealed a well-defined crystalline structure and a uniform spherical morphology. The electrochemical response of the sensor was studied over the concentration range of 10–150 µM and a linear response was obtained with a sensitivity of 0.18921 µA µM−1 and a detection limit of 8.5 µM. Overall, the CuFe2O4-modified tyrosinase electrode demonstrated sensitive electrochemical detection of tyrosine, offering a simple and effective biosensing platform for biochemical and clinical monitoring applications.
